question: Let $A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & p \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$, $B = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ q & 1 \end{bmatrix}$. For which $p, q$ is $AB = BA$? Justify your answer with matrix computation.
explanation:
Compute $AB$ and $BA$:

$AB = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & p \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ q & 1 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 1+pq & p \\ q & 1 \end{bmatrix}$

$BA = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ q & 1 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} 1 & p \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & p \\ q & qp+1 \end{bmatrix}$

Set $AB = BA$, so all entries are equal.

Set $(1,1)$: $1+pq=1 \implies pq=0$

$(1,2)$: $p=p$ always

$(2,1)$: $q=q$ always

$(2,2)$: $1=1+pq \implies pq=0$ (already addressed)

Therefore, $pq=0\implies p=0$ or $q=0$ or both.
